summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 12, part 60) set during a tense evening in a household. Lexy sits reading while Dr. Quelton and Captain Grey play silent chess and Mrs. Quelton lies idle on a chaise longue. Lexy is weighed down by guilt because she secretly replaced the contents of a tonic bottle with water, and she fears the doctor will soon discover the substitution and that Mrs. Quelton's condition may change.
one_line: Lexy, tormented by guilt after secretly swapping a drug for water, endures a tense evening with Dr. and Mrs. Quelton and Captain Grey.
key_facts: Dr. Quelton and Captain Grey are playing chess at a small table in a haze of tobacco smoke, silent and intent.
Mrs. Quelton lies on her chaise longue doing nothing at all and answers Lexy in a low but cheerful tone.
Lexy finds the evening the most wearisome and depressing she has ever spent.
A sense of guilt lies like lead upon Lexy's heart, and she is afraid of what might result from her actions.
Lexy has a chill suspicion that Dr. Quelton is watching her in turn.
Lexy thinks, "Of course, he's bound to find out some time," and expected a day or two at the very most.
Earlier, Dr. Quelton tapped the bottle and told Captain Grey that a preparation in it would make his fortune, if he chose.
Just before dinner Lexy ran up to the cupola, emptied the bottle's contents into the sink, and refilled it from the tap.
Lexy overheard the two men talking, which gave her the idea to destroy the drug that so horribly affected Mrs. Quelton.
The liquid in the bottle was colorless and almost without odor, which made the substitution easier to hide.
Lexy had meant to wait and watch until Mrs. Quelton had at least a chance to return to a normal condition.
Lexy recalls Mandy, an engineer living in Firminy, and contrasts this evening with the dullness she has felt at the Enderbys' before.
